# systemd `OnFailure=` drop-ins — data server

Every unit here posts a red Discord embed via `ktp-systemd-alert@` when it fails. Together they are
the whole failure-alerting path for the data server.

These lived **only** on the data server until 2026-08-15, while each file's own header claimed
*"Auto-generated by KTPInfrastructure ktp-systemd-alert wiring."* No generator existed and nothing
was tracked, so a host rebuild would have silently restored every service with **no alerting on any
of them** — and nothing would have noticed, because `provision/expected-timers.conf` states the data
server is not in the audit host list.

## Restore after a rebuild

```bash
# from a checkout of this repo, on the data server
sudo cp -r scripts/systemd/dropins/*.service.d /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
```

## Verify — `systemctl show`, never a grep of the unit file

```bash
systemctl show <unit> -p OnFailure --value    # must name ktp-systemd-alert@<unit>.service
```

⚠️ **A grep of the unit file is not a check.** `ktp-hlstatsx-ingest-monitor.service` and
`ktp-stats-export.service` each carry a *comment* claiming the wiring — *"fires the existing
ktp-systemd-alert OnFailure wiring — that is the whole delivery path"* — while the directive itself
was absent. Both greps hit, both units alerted nobody, and one of them had been failing hourly.
`systemctl show` resolves drop-ins and reports what systemd will actually do; the file does not.

Carry a control when checking: `hltv-demo-renamer.service` has always been correctly wired, so a
sweep that reports it as empty is a broken sweep, not a finding.

## Known inconsistency

`hud-observer` and `hud-observer-web` use `onfailure.conf`; everything else uses
`00-ktp-onfailure-alert.conf`. Both work — systemd reads every `.conf` in a `.d/` directory — but a
sweep keyed on the common filename misses those two. Match on the directory, not the filename.

## Not covered here

`ktp-render-banlist.service` has **no** drop-in and is deliberately absent from this set — see its
TODO card. It is the last unwired unit on the box.
